Hi Sofia / Vanessa — thanks for sending the samples. I've sketched a pragmatic, minimal-risk plan below so we can start moving during your narrow rollout window next week. High level: baseline -> eval harness -> canary -> full roll.

1) Baseline and mapping (Day 0–1)- We run your prompt set through the eval harness to produce: confusion matrix, intent F1, token-level anomalies, and per-prompt latency distribution. (Deliverable: baseline report + artifacts)

2) Eval harness integration (Day 1–3)- Ben will run the harness against the staged model variant you'll host with us. We will: ingest prompts as a batch, execute deterministic seeds where applicable, and store per-example outputs in the QMon datastore for comparison.

3) Canary policy & thresholds (Day 3)- Proposed matrix (we'll attach a structured sheet):
  * Core intent F1: soft-alert at -3%, hard-rollback at -5%
  * Top-1 label drift: soft-alert at 4%, hard-rollback at 7%
  * Latency p95: soft-alert at +15%, hard-fallback to lower-capacity variant at +30%
  * Toxicity / safety hits: immediate hard-rollback on any production hit above 0.1% in-sample

4) Regression alerts + actions- Soft alerts trigger a runbook task and a 2-hour response SLA for initial triage. Hard rollback auto-switches routing to the previous pinned model variant and opens a Sev2 ticket to the implementation squad.

5) Rollback playbook (Day 3–4)- Automated rollback is managed via route policy; we'll add a human confirmation gate for the first two canaries, then move to automated if stability looks good. Runbook will list pager contacts, on-call schedule, and how to escalate to your SREs.

6) Acceptance criteria for go/no-go- Baseline report reviewed, canary run produces <3% false positive alert rate on held-out prompts, and runbook acknowledged by Halcyon contacts.

I'll attach the canary_matrix_v1.xlsx and a one-page QMon acceptance template to this thread. Ben — can you confirm the expected time to ingest the CSV and run the harness for a 1k prompt sample? Grace — please confirm who from Halcyon should receive pager notifications.

Marissa / team — quick technical confirm:

- For a 1k-prompt CSV we expect the eval harness baseline run to complete in ~6 hours on a single DED-XL worker. If you want results in 72 hours we have ample slack. For the full set (5–10k) plan on 18–30 hours depending on token counts.
- We'll push outputs into the QMon store as JSONL and create diff snapshots for the canary window. The ingestion is batched and idempotent; we accept CSVs or Google Sheets exports.
- Canary automation: the route policy supports 3 stages — candidate, canary (10–20% traffic), and full pool. Rollback is a single API call; for the first two canaries we will require a manual confirmation in the Redwood Console (checkbox + approver). After three successful canaries within your SLA window we can flip to automated rollback.

I'll start the baseline run after Sofia confirms we're good to ingest the CSV.
